- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 1.5% from prior high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +1.0% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.4) over 3+ days, model overestimates upward momentum; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); adjust forecast by +0.5–1.0% for first 2–3 days of new sentiment direction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.0), model often fails to recognize; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in 3 consecutive days → model overfits noise; smooth forecast by reducing volatility in 3-day moving average.
